origin.description: Print method for an object of class "saddle.distn".

arguments.text: Further arguments passed to or from other methods.

origin.details: The quantiles are printed with the original call, the number of spline points, and the range of those points. Lugannani-Rice approximations are noted when they were used. The number of digits follows the magnitude of the middle of the range.
origin.example:
air.t0 <- c(mean(aircondit$hours), sqrt(var(aircondit$hours)/12))
air <- saddle.distn(A = cbind(aircondit$hours/12, 1), u = 12, wdist = "p",
                    type = "cond", t0 = air.t0)
print(air)

translation.description: Print the quantiles of a saddlepoint distribution approximation and return that text.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A dict as returned by saddle_distn, with quantiles, points, call, and LR.

arguments.name: unused
arguments.text: Ignored. Present so extra arguments do not raise.

translation.details: Digits follow the R rule: the ceiling of the log10 of the midpoint of the point range, then 4, 4 minus that, or 0. Halves are rounded to even. The call line is whatever string is stored in call.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from boot.data_sets import aircondit
from boot.saddle import print_saddle_distn, saddle_distn

hours = aircondit()[1][:, 0]
air_t0 = np.array([hours.mean(), np.sqrt(np.var(hours, ddof=1) / 12)])
air = saddle_distn(
    A=np.column_stack([hours / 12, np.ones(len(hours))]),
    u=12,
    wdist="p",
    type="cond",
    t0=air_t0,
)
print_saddle_distn(air)
